state.instructions: Judge the supplied heartbeat architecture choices as a classifier. Base the result on the written evidence rather than outside knowledge, assumed APIs, or a claim that agreement establishes execution.
state.facts: Adoption is canlang's priority; simplicity and efficient authored tokens serve it. The human requested first-class Cloudflare support, not a CanCheck-specific DO architecture. A provisional assistant requirement nevertheless assigns configuration/history to D1 and check timing/health to DOs. Existing declarations place Check and Transition alongside D1 Employee and Location. One mutation must use one authoritative owner under DESIGN; DO containment moves a related group together and mutable queries to another owner have no atomic guarantee. Actual pause/resume guards call can_work as quoted, and its employee-location facts are not covered by the role/active-membership context snapshot. The unbuilt D1 runtime specifies optimistic revision fencing plus a rollback-safe batch. It also specifies common D1 scheduled-work dispatch; DO alarms are another existing placement-dependent path. No contention or latency results are available. Required business behavior includes acknowledgement only after stored ping acceptance, first/subsequent missed deadlines, grace and recovery, pause/resume, persistent timer revisions, delivery correlation distinct from health, history lifetime and developer-only provisioning outside UI/MCP. Maintenance must obey owner commit/fence semantics. A D1-only authoritative group can represent this full behavior.

storage.instructions: Pick a proportionate source/requirements fix, taking account of authorization equivalence, consistency, adoption cost and the lack of performance evidence.

criteria.d1: Leave the authoritative check and related transition/notice records at D1, with the existing location permission evaluation, and amend the mistaken draft split-storage sentence. Schedule through the standard due-work dispatcher. This is smaller than inventing another grant path, while database fence contention and timer lag remain unmeasured limitations.
criteria.do_snapshot: Rehome all check-owned records together in one DO per check and introduce explicit admission snapshots of D1 employee location grants. This offers isolated ordering and direct alarms, but creates a new access contract and cannot retain atomic Employee revocation at the check owner.
criteria.defer: Report ownership as unresolved rather than changing the draft architecture now. It avoids a premature performance conclusion, yet leaves the known contradictory split requirement and delays completion despite a viable existing D1 model.
